analysis.investment_thesis: SHRIKANHA fails the Magic Formula on the quality side: ROE of 0.62% signals near-zero returns on capital, making the apparently cheap P/E of 4.48 a likely value trap rather than a bargain. A cheap price on a bad business is not what we're looking for.
key_strengths: P/E of 4.48 implies surface-level earnings yield ~22% — looks cheap on that single metric
Promoter holding of 68.59% shows skin in the game
Stainless steel cold-rolled strips is a defined niche with some specialization
key_risks: ROE of 0.62% is catastrophically low — ROIC is almost certainly well below the 20% Magic Formula threshold
No debt data provided; EV could be much higher than market cap of INR 25.90 Cr, making true earnings yield far lower than P/E implies
Commoditized, capital-intensive steel products manufacturing — structural barrier to high ROIC
red_flags: Critical data inconsistency: P/E of 4.48 implies net income of ~INR 5.78 Cr, but ROE of 0.62% implies equity of ~INR 932 Cr — these numbers cannot coexist, signaling unreliable data
Micro-cap at INR 25.90 Cr market cap — extreme illiquidity, wide bid-ask spreads, no institutional coverage
Incorporated July 2015 — less than a decade of operating history, no proven cycle resilience
FII holding of 0.03% — no institutional validation whatsoever
analysis.detailed_analysis:
The Magic Formula demands two things simultaneously: a cheap price (high earnings yield) AND a high-quality business (high ROIC). SHRIKANHA fails decisively on quality. A ROE of 0.62% tells us this business is generating almost no return on shareholder capital — in a capital-intensive, commodity-priced steel products business, that's expected. There is no pricing power, no switching costs, and no durable competitive advantage in cold-rolled stainless steel strips. The P/E of 4.48 superficially looks attractive, but without debt figures, the true EBIT/EV earnings yield is unknown — and a commodity steel business almost certainly carries working capital debt, compressing the real yield.

The internal data inconsistency is the most alarming flag: P/E of 4.48 on a INR 25.90 Cr market cap implies net income of ~INR 5.78 Cr, yet a ROE of 0.62% would require equity of ~INR 932 Cr to produce that income — an obvious impossibility. This suggests either stale data, restated financials, or a P/E computed off a historical earnings spike, none of which inspire confidence. At this scale (INR 25.90 Cr market cap), liquidity is essentially nonexistent. This stock does not belong in a Magic Formula screen.
